hypothesis: Choosing excitation probes as a minimum separating family of the candidates still consistent with the data (a hitting-set problem solved exactly) identifies an unknown plant as efficiently as greedy information-gain probing, far faster than random probing, and with a bounded worst case.
mechanism: N=64 candidate plants; candidate c = 'component c is faulty'. A library of P=48 probes; probe p exercises a fixed subset E_p of components, |E_p| uniform in {2,4,8,16,32}, members uniform; the library is regenerated until it separates every pair of candidates. Response of the plant to probe p is 1 iff its faulty component is in E_p (noise-free). The agent keeps the version space V of candidates consistent with all responses and stops when |V| = 1; a probe is never repeated. TREATMENT (Yoneda / hitting-set probing): at each step, over the current V, solve exactly (SAT or ILP with a cardinality objective) for a minimum-size set of unapplied probes that separates every pair of candidates in V (every pair is 'hit' by a probe containing exactly one of the two); apply the lowest-index probe of that set that splits V; re-solve after each response.
intervention: Hitting-set separating-family probe choice versus the reference and null policies on the same 10 libraries, every candidate taken as the true plant once per library (640 episodes per arm).
control: GREEDY_REF: greedy information gain -- the unapplied probe maximising the binary entropy of the split of V (ties: lowest index). This is the simpler alternative named for M4.
positive_control: Truth oracle: the unapplied probe whose realised response removes the most candidates (ties: lowest index). It uses the hidden truth, so it is an upper bound, not a legitimate policy; attainability of S1 by a legitimate policy is checked separately against the entropy bound (mean probes >= log2 64 = 6).
observable: Probes applied until |V| = 1, per episode, recomputable by replaying the logged (probe, response) trace against the library and the truth.

success_clauses.text: Mean probes to identification (640 episodes) is at most 1.05 x the GREEDY_REF mean on the same episodes (parity with greedy information gain).
95th percentile of probes to identification over the 640 episodes <= 8 (bounded worst case, the property a separating family is meant to buy).

failure_clauses.text: Hitting-set probing is materially worse than greedy information gain: mean probes ratio to GREEDY_REF >= 1.15.
Hitting-set probing is not clearly better than random: mean probes(X) >= 0.75 x mean probes(NULL_TWIN) (disjoint from S2: 0.75 x 13.18 = 9.89 > 9.0).
Worst case not bounded: p95 probes >= 10.

alternative_explanation: Any policy that prefers balanced splits identifies the plant near the entropy bound on a random library; a separating-family solver may do so only because its chosen family happens to contain balanced probes, i.e. it is greedy information gain by another route, and the Yoneda framing adds a name, not a mechanism. Conversely a minimum separating family is a worst-case (non-adaptive) object and may spend probes that an adaptive greedy policy would skip, making it strictly worse in the mean.
null_twin: Random probing: a uniformly random unapplied probe at each step, same libraries, same truths, same stop rule (probe choice destroyed).
why_this_implementation: Fault localisation by excitation probes is the smallest identification-by-excitation plant in which the candidate is determined by its response profile (the representable-functor reading of M4) and version spaces are exact. Probe subsets of mixed size make random probes low-information (twin mean 13.2 probes vs bound 6), fixing the flaw where every policy collapses the version space in 2-3 observations. No learned model is involved.
size: 64 candidates, 48 probes per library, 10 libraries (seeds), 64 episodes per library per arm
cost_estimate: controls: 0.16 CPU core-seconds for 4 arms; treatment: 640 episodes x <= ~10 exact minimum-hitting-set solves on <= 2016 pairs x 48 probes; expected < 3 CPU core-minutes in pure Python with a small branch-and-bound or a SAT cardinality encoding
stupid_explanations: greedy information gain already sits at the entropy bound (6.02 vs 6.0), so any balanced-split rule 'matches greedy' and S1 tests nothing specific to separating families
the minimum separating family is re-solved after every response, so the treatment is adaptive greedy in disguise; its first probe is whatever the solver's tie-break picks
S3 passes for any sensible policy because the libraries contain size-32 probes that halve V; the worst-case bound comes from the library, not the solver
random probing is a strawman: excluding never-splitting probes from the twin alone would halve its count
